title: Latency vs Quality Topology Scan for Batching & KV Cache Configs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: build a repeatable scan that quantifies the latency-quality frontier across realistic batching and KV cache topologies and yields clear rollout guardrails. This ticket defines the matrix, data sampling strategy, evaluation metrics, and automation to run nightly scans and surface regressions to the Console. The scan focuses on config knobs customers commonly change: max_batch_size, batching_window_ms, microbatch_size, prefix_cache_ttl_ms, kv_cache_lookup_shard_count, and eager_cache_fill. We will test combinations across two model families (open-llama-13B and redwood-3B-compat) with representative prompt sets (conversational, summarization, code-complete).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible experiment runner that executes the matrix and stores results in /benchmarks/latency-quality/2026-03-10/
Nightly scan job configured in CI that uploads metrics and artifacts to the metrics bucket and creates a PR if quality drops exceed thresholds
Dashboard tile in Console showing p50/p95 latency vs quality delta with drilldown to config rows and per-prompt breakdown
Alert rule: any config with >=2% absolute drop in similarity_score or >=10% increase in p95 latency flagged for review
test_plan: Matrix generation: full factorial across 3 batching_window_ms values (5, 20, 50), 3 max_batch_size values (8, 32, 128), microbatch_size (1,4), prefix_cache_ttl_ms (0,60000), kv_cache_shard_count (1,4)
For each cell run 500 requests per prompt type (conversational, summarization, code) sampled from prod-like playback corpus; hold out 10% for statistical validation

Measure: token-level generation latency (p50/p95), end-to-end request latency, throughput (tokens/s), and quality metrics: embedding_similarity to gold answer, exact-match for code snippets, semantic-ROUGE for summarization
Compute delta against baseline config (batching_window_ms=5, max_batch_size=8, prefix_cache_ttl_ms=60000) and record effect sizes with 95% CI
Run paired statistical tests (bootstrap and paired t-test where applicable) and capture significance flags
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Initial matrix defined and small smoke runner implemented; validated harness can replay 100 requests against local runtime with mocked KV cache
2026-02-22: Added embedding-similarity metric to eval harness; integrated evals-runner v0.9 which supports parallelized prompt shards
2026-03-02: Discovered non-linear latency amplification when microbatch_size > 1 with certain kernel selection paths on A100; captured kernel traces and escalated to runtime team
2026-03-07: Implemented nightly CI job prototype that runs a reduced slice of matrix and uploads metrics CSV to s3://redwood-benchmarks/latency-quality/nightly/
2026-03-10: First full-sweep run completed for redwood-3B-compat; preliminary results show a 1.8% average similarity drop at batching_window_ms=50 for conversational prompts with 32 max_batch_size
review_feedback: PM review (Elena Park): request clarifying acceptance thresholds and prefer absolute quality loss thresholds per workload type rather than single global threshold
Design review (Rajiv Desai): dashboard should surface the minimal changes that recover quality (e.g., reduce batching_window_ms or reduce microbatch) so runbook automations can be created
Security review (Maya Chen): ensure eval corpus is scrubbed of PII before upload and that artifacts in S3 are access-restricted
next_steps: Triage the top 5 config rows that show >1.5% quality loss and p95 latency <= baseline+20% to identify low-risk optimizations
Add automated rollback safety rules into rollout service: if nightly scan flags a regression for a recently deployed config, block canary completion
Coordinate with runtime team for a microkernel patch that reduces latency amplification seen at microbatch_size > 1
Finalize Console dashboard wire and schedule a design review on 2026-03-16
